study.question: Observed limitation: sharing positional logits with joint gradients gave click AUC 0.6640206391 (g3-r0015-position_shared_joint), versus 0.6654978909 with the same shared forward and primary-only positional gradients. Position residuals with protected event donation gave 0.6654921504 and joint donation 0.6640205217; protected mean donation 0.6655004756 did not improve the incumbent 0.6655420609. Are opposing auxiliary gradient directions on the useful shared positional representation responsible for part of this loss, and can a restricted non-opposing auxiliary update outperform complete exclusion? These observations do not measure gradient conflict directly.
study.hypothesis: At some training batches the aggregate auxiliary BCE gradient on the single shared positional coefficient tensor opposes the click gradient. Preserve the click gradient and remove only the opposing component of the aggregate auxiliary gradient. If auxiliary information has complementary directions, this route-local projection should recover click quality relative to joint sharing and improve over complete auxiliary exclusion. A direction-preserving control with the same retained auxiliary norm tests whether simple attenuation explains the result. This is a hypothesis about pre-clipping backward information flow through one existing unified route, not a population descent guarantee.

study.proposed_difference: All four variants use the exact same shared/joint forward graph. Define p=dL_click/dW and a=d(sum L_aux)/dW for existing position_gate_weight W, with two retained-graph autograd.grad probes (no .grad writes or forward replay). In FP32 let u=p/||p|| when nonzero, else0; a_proj=a-min(<a,u>,0)u. Project cell uses a_proj, norm cell uses a*min(1,||a_proj||/||a||) with zero-safe denominator, joint cell uses a, primary cell uses0. The zero-valued detached linear surrogate changes dL/dW from p+a to p+a_selected while preserving the scalar sum of four BCEs and all other leaf gradients before clipping. Labels are consumed only by training_loss. The claim is restricted gradient geometry on the existing route, not a new forward architecture or an original optimization algorithm.
predictions: At identical finite weights/inputs and FeatureMap task order, all four outputs and scalar losses agree exactly; before clipping, every non-positional parameter gradient agrees within numerical tolerance. No optimizer/.grad mutation or repeated forward occurs.

For finite nonzero p, <p,a_proj> is nonnegative within FP32 tolerance; ||a_proj||<=||a||, and norm cell preserves the direction of a and matches its retained norm. p=0 keeps a, a=0 yields0. Positive alignment leaves a unchanged. All-empty/zero-length histories yield zero positional correction without NaNs.

Directional explanation: position_gradient_project improves click validation AUC over position_gradient_norm and position_gradient_joint. Complementarity additionally requires improvement over position_gradient_primary and the incumbent; matching primary only supports safe suppression, not useful auxiliary transfer.

Predeclared practical follow-up trigger: >=0.0002 click AUC over both the new primary and norm controls, with no explanation by endpoint-hook mismatch, warrants paired-seed follow-up. This heuristic is not a significance threshold. Report all four AUC/Logloss, auxiliary mean separately, parameter counts, wall/allocated GPU seconds, peak memory and inference metrics whether favorable or not.

Use existing history bins empty/1-16/17-64/>64 and their validation counts/positive/negative counts as predeclared diagnostics; earlier positional gains were larger in 17-64 and >64. Empty-history shifts can arise indirectly from shared context/clipping and are not direct position effects. Other slices are exploratory unless frozen in host protocol. Any unavailable user-cluster uncertainty/gradient statistics must be reported unavailable, never invented.

falsifiers: If the joint hook does not match the shared/joint endpoint at fixed-state value/gradient checks, or the primary hook fails to match the shared/primary endpoint pre-clipping gradients, suspend mechanism interpretation and diagnose the hook before using archived endpoints. No silently changed loss stabilization or host recipe is allowed.
If project does not outperform norm at matched forward/capacity/probe cost, directional removal is unsupported; norm-equivalent recovery is consistent with attenuation alone.

If project beats joint but not primary, useful auxiliary contribution beyond exclusion is unsupported. If all are below the incumbent, retain the incumbent; the frozen proposal is not a model-selection success.

If forward, backward, masking, arbitrary-task-order, BF16 or finite-loss checks fail, classify as implementation failure with charged cost, not scientific refutation. If the unit cap is reached, stop that trial without changing the cap.

Even a favorable single-seed AUC cannot establish a general mechanism; reproducibility, gradient invariants and future paired seeds are required. No claim of universal absence/presence of negative transfer, convergence, production validity or novelty follows.
alternative_explanations: The Euclidean constraint applies before global dense clipping and AdamW preconditioning; it does not guarantee the actual parameter step or click AUC improves
Shared context gradients, pooled-score dependence and global clipping remain task couplings; changes in their trajectories are downstream effects
Aggregate auxiliary gradients can hide conflicts among cart/fav/buy; direction and norm are measured in redundant allocated positional coordinates

Single fixed training seed and repeated validation-guided research: differences are preliminary and subject to selection bias; user-cluster uncertainty/paired seeds need future authorized host support

Prior trajectories include useful primary selector/item gradient isolation, auxiliary ranking collapse without private items (g3-r0003-embedding_item_primary), harmful auxiliary event donation (g3-r0012-redistrib_aux_live), and no click benefit from recent auxiliary residual donation. They concern different routes and do not prove all auxiliary training is harmful. All historical trials shown are execution successes; negative scientific findings must not be relabeled execution failures.

Feedback identities on position coefficients were near-null while event-vs-marginal position mattered (g3-r0014-position_collapsed0.6655081614 vs marginal0.6638023790). Projection might recover a better rank prior without learning complementary feedback. Norm control and primary endpoint discriminate only part of this explanation.

Current authorized registry supplies no primary gradient-surgery paper; closest optimization precedent remains unverified. This is an empirical adaptation with no novelty score. Previously declared industry usage is provenance, not causal evidence: g3-r0016 joint donation was worse and its protected variants did not beat the incumbent.
